The horizontal component of any vector is found with the cosine of its angle measured from the horizontal, \( \text{component}= \text{magnitude}\times\cos\theta\) [2]. In the example in the text a 20 m vector at 60° north of east gives an eastward component of \(20\cos60^\circ =10\) m, showing the same cosine rule applies regardless of the vector’s size [1]. Applying that rule to the 40 m displacement:  

\[
\text{East‑ward component}=40\cos60^\circ =40\times0.5 =20\ \text{m}.
\]

A result of 34.6 m would come from using \(\sin60^\circ\) instead of \(\cos60^\circ\), which is the common error noted in the material.
